sanskrit: āyam agan saṃvatsaraḥ patir ekāṣṭake tava | tasmai devāya haviṣā vidhema sa u naḥ śarma yacchatu ||
english: The year has come, O Ekāṣṭakā, as your lord. To that deity we would do homage with oblation; may he grant us shelter.

sanskrit: ekāṣṭakāyai haviṣā vidhema ya rtūn pañcānu praviṣṭā | sasyena sasyam upasaṃcaranto ariṣṭāsa ṛtuna rtum upa saṃ carema ||
english: With oblation we would honor Ekāṣṭakā who has entered the five seasons one by one; passing from crop to crop — unharmed, may we pass from season to season.

sanskrit: vasanto grīṣmo madhumanta varṣāḥ śarad dhemanta ṛtavo no juṣantām | ā no goṣu bhajantv ā prajāyāṃ suśarmaṇy eṣāṃ trivarūthe syāma ||
english: Spring, summer, honey-sweet rains, autumn, winter — may the seasons delight in us. May they grant us a share in cattle and in offspring; may we abide in their good shelter, in their triple refuge.

sanskrit: ekāṣṭakā tapasā tapyamānā jajāna garbhaṃ mahimānam indram | tena devā vy aṣahanta śatrūn hantāsurāṇām abhavac chacīpatiḥ ||
english: Ekāṣṭakā, glowing with the heat of austerity, gave birth to the embryo of greatness — Indra. With him the gods overcame enemies; he became the slayer of asuras, the lord of Śacī.

sanskrit: pūrṇā darve parā pata supūrṇā punar ā pata | sarvān yajñān saṃ pṛñcati- -iṣam ūrjaṃ na ā bhara ||
english: Full ladle, fly forth! Fully full, fly back again! It mingles together all sacrifices — bring us refreshment and strength.

sanskrit: iṣam ūrjaṃ na ābhṛtya- -iḍayā paśubhiḥ saha | sarasvati tvam asmāsu rāyaspoṣaṃ ni yaccha ||
english: Having brought refreshment and strength to us together with Iḍā and cattle — O Sarasvatī, bestow upon us abundance of wealth.

sanskrit: vātasya nu mahimā rathasya- -ārujann eti stanayann asya ghoṣaḥ | divaspṛg ety aruṇāni kṛṇvann atho eti pṛthivyā reṇum asyan ||
english: Now the greatness of the Wind, of the chariot — crashing it comes; thundering is its roar. Touching the sky it makes things ruddy; then it goes, hurling the dust of earth.

sanskrit: saṃ prerate anu vātasya viṣṭhā ainaṃ gacchanti samaneva yoṣāḥ | tābhir vidvān sarathaṃ deva īyate patir viśvasya bhuvanasya gopāḥ ||
english: The swaths of the wind rush together; they come toward him as women to an assembly. Knowing them, the god moves on the same chariot — the lord, the guardian of all the world.

sanskrit: ātmā devānāṃ bhuvanasya gopā yathāvaśaṃ carati deva eṣaḥ | ghoṣa id asya śrūyate na rūpaṃ tasmai devāya haviṣā vidhema ||
english: The soul of the gods, the guardian of the world — this god moves as he wills. Only his roar is heard, not his form; to that god we would do homage with oblation.

sanskrit: antarikṣe pathibhir īyamāno na ni viśate katamac canāhaḥ | apāṃ yoniḥ prathamajā ṛtasya kva svij jātaḥ kuta ā babhūva ||
english: Traveling in the atmosphere by his paths, he does not settle in any day whatsoever. The womb of waters, first-born of cosmic order (ṛta) — where indeed was he born, whence did he arise?

sanskrit: antarikṣe patayantaṃ vāta tvām āśum āśubhiḥ | paśyanti sarve cakṣuṣā na sarve manasā viduḥ ||
english: O Vāta, flying swiftly through the atmosphere with swift [forces] — all see you with their eyes; not all know you with their mind.

sanskrit: upatrikaṃ saṃcavicaṃ triryamaṃ caturekajam | taṃ mātariśvānaṃ devaṃ divo devā avāsṛjan ||
english: The one that moves in threes, that converges in threes, that is yoked in threes, that makes four into one — that god Mātariśvan the gods of heaven released abroad.

sanskrit: apa ny adhuḥ pauruṣeyaṃ vadhaṃ mad indrāgnī dhātā savitā bṛhaspatiḥ | somo rājā varuṇo aśvinā yamaḥ pūṣāsmān pari pātu mṛtyoḥ ||
english: Indra and Agni, Dhātṛ, Savitṛ, Bṛhaspati have put away from me the man-slaying stroke. King Soma, Varuṇa, the two Aśvins, Yama, Pūṣan — may they protect us from death.

sanskrit: yāni cakāra bhuvanasya yas patiḥ prajāpatir mātariśvā prajābhyaḥ | pradiśo yāni vasate diśaś ca tāni me varmāṇi bahulāni santu ||
english: Whatever the lord of the world, Prajāpati, Mātariśvan, has fashioned for creatures — the intermediate quarters where one dwells, and the cardinal directions — may those many armors be mine.

sanskrit: yat tanuṣv anahyanta devā dvirājayodhinaḥ | indro yac cakre varma tad asmān pātu viśvataḥ ||
english: What the gods, fighting in the battle of two kings, bound upon their bodies — the armor that Indra made — may that protect us from all sides.

sanskrit: varma me dyāvāpṛthivī varmāhar varma sūryaḥ | varma me viśve devāḥ kran mā mā prāpat pratīcikā ||
english: May heaven and earth be armor for me; armor the day; armor the sun. May all the gods make armor for me; may the counter-stroke not reach me.
